lines: He is sitting on an equipment crate with a module panel across his knees, not working on it.
"Rike Halloran. Salvage. Mostly I catalogue things that used to work."
"You will want the recycler first. Everything else is comfort; that one is arithmetic."
"Two jobs. The intake is packed solid - cut it out, patch the housing, four plate and a couple of fibre."
"Then the filter stack wants fresh glass and something living to prime it. A lumen pod does it. Do not ask me why a vegetable primes an air scrubber, ask the people who designed it."
"Plate you can cut off the wrecked sections around the apron. Glass comes out of the hollow, or off the terrace edge if you do not fancy the walk."
"Officially? Cascade failure, environmental collapse, crew evacuated on foot and did not make it."
"Unofficially, I have had that panel open for a year." He taps it. "Nothing in it is broken."
"The comms anchors were cut. Cut, square, with a torch, by somebody who took their time. The signal board was removed and it is not in the debris because it was carried away."
"That is not a disaster. That is a decision, and I do not like not knowing whose."
"Do me a favour while you are out there scavenging."
"I keep a ledger of every part the old crew pulled. Eight plate and a couple of cells and I can weigh what is missing against what is merely broken."
"I want to be able to prove the difference. To myself, mostly."

choices.text: I will bring you the stock.

lines: "Eight plate, two cells. Take the torch to the wrecked sections, they are still full of both."
"Fair. The ledger has waited a year, it can wait a week."
"Eight plate, two cells. I will be here."
"Dish is up. I pulled the outbound queue first thing."
He turns the slate around. It is empty.
"Four years of a working transmitter and not one outbound packet. No mayday, no status ping, nothing."
"People in trouble reach for the radio. It is the first thing you do. They did not do it, which means they were not in trouble."
"They were doing something else."
"You want to know the part that keeps me up."

"Every single thing they disabled, they disabled reversibly. Anchors cut clean so they can be re-welded. Board pulled, not smashed. Hydroponics head unbolted and set down on a cloth, on a cloth, so the threads would not take grit."
"You do not do that to a machine you are abandoning. You do that to a machine you expect someone to come back to."
"They left us a door. I would very much like to know what is on the other side of choosing to walk through it."
"Straun. It was Straun who did the disabling, and she voted against."
"She lost the argument and then she spent her last two weeks making sure the loser's case stayed on the table."
He is quiet for a moment. "That is the most engineer thing I have ever heard."
"Torch cuts salvage. Scanner tells you what a module is missing before you haul the wrong thing across the apron."
"Use the scanner. Saves walking."
